gloss: look at or read something again carefully
example: Go over your introduction before you start the body paragraphs.
antNote: No exact opposite: these words mean not looking carefully enough.

gloss: look at or read something very carefully to find every detail
thai: ตรวจสอบอย่างละเอียด
example: Examiners scrutinise every paragraph for a clear line of argument.
antNote: No exact opposite: these words mean looking quickly or not at all.

gloss: do something too quickly and without enough care
example: If you rush the conclusion, you may forget to restate your position.
antNote: No exact opposite: these words mean taking time to work carefully.

gloss: not do or read something that you should
example: Never skip the planning stage, even when time is short.
antNote: No exact opposite: these words mean reading something carefully instead of missing it.

gloss: fail to notice or think about something
example: Many students overlook small errors with words like 'a' and 'the'.

gloss: willing to listen to and accept new or different ideas
example: An open-minded writer considers the other side before giving her view.

gloss: able to change easily to fit new situations
thai: ปรับตัวได้ดี
example: An adaptable student can use one plan for many types of question.

gloss: able to do many different things or be used in many ways
example: A versatile writer can argue, describe and compare with equal skill.

gloss: not able or willing to change
example: Don't use a fixed template for every question; adapt it to the task.

gloss: refusing to change your ideas, even when you should
example: A stubborn writer ignores the other side, so the essay feels one-sided.

gloss: very strict and not able to change or bend
thai: ไม่ยืดหยุ่น
example: Rigid templates make every essay sound the same.

gloss: the ability to make new and original ideas
thai: ความคิดสร้างสรรค์
example: Her essay shows real creativity: the example is her own, not a textbook one.
antNote: No exact opposite: these words name taking ideas from others instead of making new ones.

gloss: learned so well that you can say it without looking
thai: ท่องจำขึ้นใจ
example: She had learnt the opening sentence by heart, so it sounded stiff.
antNote: No exact opposite: these words describe language made up fresh at the moment.

gloss: approved by people in charge, and used in serious situations
thai: เป็นทางการ
example: The official instructions say the essay must be at least 250 words.

gloss: the places or people that information first comes from
example: A good writer checks the origins of a fact before she uses it.
antNote: No exact opposite: these words name what comes at the end, not the beginning.
